title: 丹青引赠曹将军霸
title_en: A Song of Painting, for General Cao Ba
author: 杜甫

text_note.zh: 这里用通行本。和语料相比：第四句语料作“文彩风流犹尚存”，通行本作“文采风流今尚存”；“南熏殿”作“南薰殿”；“惨澹”作“惨淡”；“韩干”恢复为人名原字“韩幹”；“飘泊”作“漂泊”；“坎𡒄”作“坎壈”。语料把“褒公鄂公毛发动，英姿飒爽来酣战”连成了一句，这里分成两句。
text_note.en: This is the common text. Compared with the corpus: in line 4 the corpus has a different character for cǎi and yóu ('still') where the common text has jīn ('now'); the hall's name uses a different xūn character; dàn in line 22 uses the common form; Han Gan's name is restored to its original character; piāo in line 35 uses the 'drift on water' form; and the rare form of lǎn in the last line is replaced by the standard one. The corpus also runs lines 15 and 16 together; here they are split.

readings.en: Here it means 'to become', read wéi.
Here it means 'to become', read wéi.
Here it means 'many times', read shuò.

readings.zh: 良相：贤良的宰相，读 xiàng。
readings.en: In liáng xiàng, a good chief minister, it is read xiàng.

readings.zh: 猛将：勇猛的将领，读 jiàng。
readings.en: In měng jiàng, a fierce general, it is read jiàng.

readings.zh: 长风：远远吹来的大风，读 cháng。
readings.en: In cháng fēng, a long, strong wind, it is read cháng.
In jiǔ chóng, the ninefold palace, it is read chóng.

readings.zh: 韩幹是人名，读 Hán Gàn。语料把“幹”转换成了“干”，这里恢复原字，免得和“干戈”的“干”（gān）弄混。
readings.en: Han Gan is a name, read gàn. The machine conversion changed the character to the one also used for gān (shield); the original is restored here to avoid confusion.

readings.zh: 殊相：不同的样子，读 xiàng。
readings.en: In shū xiàng, different looks and poses, it is read xiàng.
In diāo sàng, to wither and be lost, it is read sàng.

glosses.zh: 将军：指曹霸。他做过左武卫将军。
glosses.en: jiāng jūn: Cao Ba, who once held the rank of a general in the palace guard.

glosses.zh: 魏武：魏武帝曹操。曹霸是曹操的后代。
glosses.en: wèi wǔ: Emperor Wu of Wei, that is, Cao Cao. Cao Ba was his descendant.

glosses.zh: 庶：平民，普通百姓。
glosses.en: shù: a commoner, an ordinary person.

glosses.zh: 清门：清寒的人家，家里穷但清白。
glosses.en: qīng mén: a poor but honest family.

glosses.zh: 割据：占据一块地方，自成一方势力。这里指曹操在三国时称雄。
glosses.en: gē jù: to hold a region as one's own power; here, Cao Cao ruling during the Three Kingdoms.

glosses.zh: 已矣：已经过去了。
glosses.en: yǐ yǐ: is over and gone.

glosses.zh: 文采风流：文学艺术上的才华和潇洒的风度。
glosses.en: wén cǎi fēng liú: a gift for art and letters, and a graceful, free spirit.

glosses.zh: 卫夫人：东晋女书法家卫铄。王羲之小时候跟她学过字。
glosses.en: wèi fū rén: Wei Shuo, a woman calligrapher of the Eastern Jin. Wang Xizhi learned writing from her as a boy.

glosses.zh: 但恨：只遗憾。
glosses.en: dàn hèn: his only regret.

glosses.zh: 无过：没能超过。
glosses.en: wú guò: could not surpass.

glosses.zh: 王右军：王羲之。他做过右军将军，人称王右军，被称为“书圣”。
glosses.en: wáng yòu jūn: Wang Xizhi, called Wang Youjun after his post, and known as the Sage of Calligraphy.

glosses.zh: 丹青：红色和青色两种颜料，代指绘画。
glosses.en: dān qīng: red and blue-green paints; it stands for painting.

glosses.zh: 不知老将至：不知道老年快要来了。出自《论语》，形容一心做事，忘了时间。
glosses.en: bù zhī lǎo jiāng zhì: not noticing old age coming on. From the Analects of Confucius; it means being so absorbed that one forgets time.

glosses.zh: 富贵于我如浮云：富贵对我来说，就像天上的浮云。也出自《论语》，意思是不看重钱财地位。
glosses.en: fù guì yú wǒ rú fú yún: wealth and rank are like floating clouds to me. Also from the Analects; it means not caring about money or status.

glosses.zh: 开元：唐玄宗的年号（713—741）。
glosses.en: kāi yuán: a reign name of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang (713–741).

glosses.zh: 引见：被带去见皇帝。
glosses.en: yǐn jiàn: to be brought before the emperor.

glosses.zh: 承恩：受到皇帝的宠爱。
glosses.en: chéng ēn: to enjoy the emperor's favor.

glosses.zh: 数上：多次登上。
glosses.en: shuò shàng: went up many times.

glosses.zh: 南薰殿：唐朝长安兴庆宫里的一座宫殿。
glosses.en: nán xūn diàn: a hall in the Xingqing Palace in Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 凌烟功臣：唐太宗让人把二十四位开国功臣的像画在凌烟阁上。凌烟阁是长安宫中的一座楼阁。
glosses.en: líng yān gōng chén: Emperor Taizong of Tang had portraits of twenty-four great founding ministers painted in the Lingyan Pavilion, a building in the palace at Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 少颜色：颜色褪了。
glosses.en: shǎo yán sè: the colors had faded.

glosses.zh: 开生面：画出新的面貌，让画像重新有了生气。成语“别开生面”就从这里来。
glosses.en: kāi shēng miàn: to give the faces new life. The idiom for 'opening up a fresh new way' comes from this.

glosses.zh: 良相：贤良的宰相。
glosses.en: liáng xiàng: good chief ministers.

glosses.zh: 进贤冠：古代文官戴的一种帽子。
glosses.en: jìn xián guān: a kind of cap worn by civil officials.

glosses.zh: 猛将：勇猛的将军。
glosses.en: měng jiàng: fierce generals.

glosses.zh: 大羽箭：尾巴上装着羽毛的大箭。
glosses.en: dà yǔ jiàn: big arrows with feathers at the tail.

glosses.zh: 褒公：褒国公段志玄，唐朝开国名将。
glosses.en: bāo gōng: Duke of Bao, Duan Zhixuan, a famous general who helped found the Tang.

glosses.zh: 鄂公：鄂国公尉迟敬德，也是唐朝开国名将。
glosses.en: è gōng: Duke of E, Yuchi Jingde, another famous founding general.

glosses.zh: 毛发动：胡须和头发好像在飘动。
glosses.en: máo fà dòng: their hair and beards seem to move.

glosses.zh: 英姿飒爽：英俊威武，精神抖擞。今天还常用这个成语。
glosses.en: yīng zī sà shuǎng: brave, handsome and full of spirit. People still use this idiom today.

glosses.zh: 酣战：打得正激烈的仗。
glosses.en: hān zhàn: fierce, all-out battle.

glosses.zh: 先帝：去世的皇帝，这里指唐玄宗。
glosses.en: xiān dì: the late emperor, here Emperor Xuanzong.

glosses.zh: 玉花骢：唐玄宗的一匹名马。骢，青白毛色相杂的马。
glosses.en: yù huā cōng: a famous horse of Emperor Xuanzong. Cōng is a horse with mixed blue-grey and white hair.

glosses.zh: 画工如山：画师多得像山一样。
glosses.en: huà gōng rú shān: painters as many as a mountain.

glosses.zh: 貌不同：画出来都不像。貌，描画。
glosses.en: mào bù tóng: none of their pictures looked like it. Mào here means to paint a likeness.

glosses.zh: 是日：那一天。
glosses.en: shì rì: that day.

glosses.zh: 赤墀：皇宫里涂成红色的台阶。
glosses.en: chì chí: the red-painted steps of the palace.

glosses.zh: 迥立：高高地站着。
glosses.en: jiǒng lì: standing tall.

glosses.zh: 阊阖：宫门。传说天宫的门叫阊阖。
glosses.en: chāng hé: the palace gate. In legend, the gate of heaven has this name.

glosses.zh: 生长风：好像带起了一阵长风，形容马很神气。
glosses.en: shēng cháng fēng: as if stirring up a long wind; the horse looks full of spirit.

glosses.zh: 诏：皇帝下命令。
glosses.en: zhào: the emperor ordered.

glosses.zh: 拂绢素：铺开白绢。绢素，白色的丝织品，用来作画。
glosses.en: fú juàn sù: to spread out white silk, which was used for painting.

glosses.zh: 意匠：作画时的构思。
glosses.en: yì jiàng: the plan in the painter's mind.

glosses.zh: 惨淡经营：费尽心思地构思和安排。成语“惨淡经营”就从这里来。
glosses.en: cǎn dàn jīng yíng: to think and plan with great effort. The idiom for working hard against difficulty comes from this.

glosses.zh: 斯须：一会儿，不久。
glosses.en: sī xū: in a moment.

glosses.zh: 九重：皇宫。皇宫的门一重又一重，所以这样叫。
glosses.en: jiǔ chóng: the palace, so called because it has gate after gate.

glosses.zh: 真龙：真正的龙马。古人把好马叫作龙。这里说画出来的马像真的神马。
glosses.en: zhēn lóng: a true dragon-horse. People of old called great horses dragons. The painted horse looks like a real heavenly horse.

glosses.zh: 一洗万古凡马空：一下子把古往今来所有平庸的马画都比下去了。
glosses.en: yī xǐ wàn gǔ fán mǎ kōng: at one stroke it washed away all the ordinary horse paintings of ten thousand years.

glosses.zh: 却在：竟然在。这里指画好的玉花骢放在御座上。
glosses.en: què zài: now stood at; the finished painting of Jade Flower was set on the emperor's couch.

glosses.zh: 御榻：皇帝坐卧的榻。
glosses.en: yù tà: the emperor's couch.

glosses.zh: 屹相向：高高地面对面站着。指画上的马和庭前的真马。
glosses.en: yì xiāng xiàng: standing tall, facing each other: the painted horse and the real one in the courtyard.

glosses.zh: 至尊：皇帝。
glosses.en: zhì zūn: the emperor.

glosses.zh: 催赐金：催人赏给黄金。
glosses.en: cuī cì jīn: urged that gold be given as a reward.

glosses.zh: 圉人：养马的人。
glosses.en: yǔ rén: grooms who looked after the horses.

glosses.zh: 太仆：管理皇家车马的官。
glosses.en: tài pú: the official in charge of the imperial horses.

glosses.zh: 惆怅：若有所失的样子。画马太像真马，他们都看呆了。
glosses.en: chóu chàng: feeling as if they had lost something; the painted horse was so real that they were stunned.

glosses.zh: 韩幹：唐代画马名家。杜甫说他是曹霸的学生。
glosses.en: hán gàn: a famous Tang painter of horses. Du Fu says he was Cao Ba's student.

glosses.zh: 入室：学到了老师的真本事。出自《论语》“升堂入室”。
glosses.en: rù shì: to have mastered the teacher's real skill. From a saying in the Analects.

glosses.zh: 穷殊相：画尽各种不同的样子。穷，尽。
glosses.en: qióng shū xiàng: to paint every kind of look and pose.

glosses.zh: 画肉不画骨：只画出马肥壮的肉，画不出马的骨力和精神。
glosses.en: huà ròu bù huà gǔ: painting only the horse's flesh, not the strength of its bones and spirit.

glosses.zh: 忍使：竟忍心让。
glosses.en: rěn shǐ: how could he bear to let.

glosses.zh: 骅骝：古代骏马的名字，泛指好马。
glosses.en: huá liú: the name of a famous steed of old; any fine horse.

glosses.zh: 气凋丧：神气衰减、丧失。
glosses.en: qì diāo sàng: lose its spirit.

glosses.zh: 盖有神：原来是因为有神韵。盖，原来是、大概是。
glosses.en: gài yǒu shén: because it has spirit; gài here means 'it is because'.

glosses.zh: 必逢佳士亦写真：一般理解为：一定要遇到品德才学好的人，才肯为他画像。写真，画人像。
glosses.en: bì féng jiā shì yì xiě zhēn: usually read as: only when he met a worthy person would he paint a portrait. Xiě zhēn means to paint a portrait.

glosses.zh: 即今：如今。
glosses.en: jí jīn: now.

glosses.zh: 漂泊：到处流浪，没有固定的家。
glosses.en: piāo bó: to wander with no settled home.

glosses.zh: 干戈：两种兵器，代指战争。
glosses.en: gān gē: two kinds of weapons; it stands for war.

glosses.zh: 屡貌：多次描画。
glosses.en: lǚ mào: often paints.

glosses.zh: 寻常行路人：普通的过路人。
glosses.en: xún cháng xíng lù rén: ordinary passers-by.

glosses.zh: 途穷：走投无路，处境困难。
glosses.en: tú qióng: at the end of one's road, in hard times.

glosses.zh: 俗眼白：被俗人用白眼看。白眼，看不起人的眼神。
glosses.en: sú yǎn bái: scornful looks from common people. Showing the whites of one's eyes is a look of contempt.

glosses.zh: 如公贫：像您这样穷。公，对曹霸的尊称。
glosses.en: rú gōng pín: as poor as you; gōng is a polite way to address Cao Ba.

glosses.zh: 盛名：很大的名气。
glosses.en: shèng míng: great fame.

glosses.zh: 坎壈：困顿，不得志。
glosses.en: kǎn lǎn: hardship and frustration.

glosses.zh: 缠其身：缠在身上，摆脱不了。
glosses.en: chán qí shēn: clings to them and will not let go.

translation.zh: 曹将军是魏武帝曹操的后代，
translation.en: General Cao is a descendant of Cao Cao, Emperor Wu of Wei.

translation.zh: 如今却成了平民，家境清寒。
translation.en: Now he is a commoner, from a poor but honest family.

translation.zh: 曹操那样的英雄割据一方，虽然已成过去，
translation.en: The days when heroes like Cao Cao held their own lands are over,

translation.zh: 曹家的文采和风度，到今天还留在他身上。
translation.en: But the family's gift for art and its grace live on in him today.

translation.zh: 他学书法，起初学的是卫夫人，
translation.en: When he learned calligraphy, he first studied Lady Wei's style.

translation.zh: 只遗憾没能超过王羲之。
translation.en: His only regret was that he could not surpass Wang Xizhi.

translation.zh: 他一心作画，连老年快要来了都不知道；
translation.en: So lost in painting, he did not notice old age coming;

translation.zh: 富贵在他看来，就像天上的浮云。
translation.en: Wealth and rank were no more to him than floating clouds.

translation.zh: 开元年间，他常常被皇上召见，
translation.en: In the Kaiyuan years he was often called before the emperor,

translation.zh: 承蒙恩宠，多次登上南薰殿。
translation.en: And, enjoying his favor, went up to the Nanxun Hall many times.

translation.zh: 凌烟阁上功臣的画像已经褪了颜色，
translation.en: The portraits of the great ministers in the Lingyan Pavilion had faded;

translation.zh: 将军一动笔，就让他们重新有了生气。
translation.en: When the general took up his brush, he gave them new life.

translation.zh: 贤良的宰相头上戴着进贤冠，
translation.en: The good ministers wear the scholar's cap on their heads;

translation.zh: 勇猛的将军腰间挂着大羽箭。
translation.en: The fierce generals carry great feathered arrows at their waists.

translation.zh: 褒公、鄂公的胡须头发好像在飘动，
translation.en: The hair and beards of the Dukes of Bao and E seem to move,

translation.zh: 英姿勃勃，好像刚从激烈的战斗中走来。
translation.en: So brave and dashing, as if just come from fierce battle.

translation.zh: 先帝有一匹天马，名叫玉花骢，
translation.en: The late emperor had a heavenly horse named Jade Flower.

translation.zh: 画师多得像山一样，画出来的却都不像它。
translation.en: Painters as many as a mountain tried, but none caught its likeness.

translation.zh: 那一天，把它牵到皇宫的红台阶下，
translation.en: That day it was led to the foot of the red palace steps.

translation.zh: 它昂首立在宫门前，好像带起一阵长风。
translation.en: It stood tall before the palace gate, as if stirring a long wind.

translation.zh: 皇上下令，让将军铺开白绢作画，
translation.en: The emperor ordered the general to spread out white silk.

translation.zh: 他用尽心思，苦心构思安排。
translation.en: He thought hard and planned the picture with great care.

translation.zh: 不一会儿，皇宫里出现了一匹真正的龙马，
translation.en: In a moment a true dragon-horse appeared in the palace,

translation.zh: 把古往今来平庸的马画全都比了下去。
translation.en: Washing away all the ordinary horse paintings of ten thousand years.

translation.zh: 画上的玉花骢竟然到了御座上，
translation.en: The painted Jade Flower now stood upon the emperor's couch;

translation.zh: 座上的画马和庭前的真马，高高地面对面站着。
translation.en: The horse on the couch and the horse in the courtyard stood tall, facing each other.

translation.zh: 皇上含笑，催人赏赐黄金，
translation.en: The emperor smiled and urged that gold be given as a reward,

translation.zh: 养马的人和管马的官，都看得若有所失。
translation.en: While the grooms and the master of horses stood stunned, as if they had lost something.

translation.zh: 他的学生韩幹，早就学到了真本事，
translation.en: His student Han Gan had long since mastered the art,

translation.zh: 也能画马，画出各种不同的姿态。
translation.en: And he too could paint horses in every kind of pose.

translation.zh: 可韩幹只画马的肉，不画马的骨，
translation.en: But Han Gan painted only flesh, not bone,

translation.zh: 竟忍心让骏马失去了神气。
translation.en: And let the fine steeds lose their spirit.

translation.zh: 将军画得好，是因为画里有神韵；
translation.en: The general's painting is great because it has spirit;

translation.zh: 一定要遇到品德好的人，他才肯为人画像。
translation.en: Only when he met a worthy person would he paint a portrait.

translation.zh: 如今在战乱中四处漂泊，
translation.en: Now he wanders in a time of war,

translation.zh: 常常给路上普通的行人画像。
translation.en: And often paints ordinary passers-by.

translation.zh: 走投无路的时候，反被俗人白眼相看，
translation.en: At the end of his road, he gets only scornful looks from common people;

translation.zh: 世上没有谁比您更穷了。
translation.en: No one in the world is as poor as you, sir.

translation.zh: 只要看看自古以来名气大的人，
translation.en: Just look at the famous people of the past:

translation.zh: 一辈子总被困苦缠着身子。
translation.en: All their days, hardship clings to them.

background.zh: 这首诗一般认为写于唐代宗广德二年（764年），当时杜甫在成都遇到了画家曹霸。曹霸是曹操的后代，唐玄宗时以画马和画人物出名，曾奉命重画凌烟阁功臣像，也给玄宗的名马画过像。后来他犯了罪，被削去官职，成了平民。安史之乱以后，他流落到四川，靠给人画像过日子。杜甫同情他的遭遇，写了这首诗送给他。“丹青”是绘画，“引”是古诗的一种体裁。
background.en: This poem is usually dated to 764, when Du Fu met the painter Cao Ba in Chengdu. Cao Ba was a descendant of Cao Cao. Under Emperor Xuanzong he was famous for painting horses and people. He was ordered to repaint the portraits of the founding ministers in the Lingyan Pavilion, and he painted the emperor's famous horse. Later he was punished, stripped of his post, and made a commoner. After the An Lushan Rebellion he drifted to Sichuan and made a living painting portraits. Du Fu felt for him and wrote this poem as a gift. Dān qīng means painting, and yǐn is a kind of old-style song.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，被称为“诗圣”。他经历了安史之乱，一生四处漂泊，写了许多反映百姓苦难的诗。他也很懂书画，写过好几首评论绘画的诗。写这首诗时，他自己也流落在成都，日子很苦，所以最后几句写曹霸穷困潦倒，其实也写了他自己。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, called the Sage of Poetry. He lived through the An Lushan Rebellion, wandered all his life, and wrote many poems about the people's suffering. He knew a lot about painting and calligraphy and wrote several poems about paintings. When he wrote this one, he too was stranded and poor in Chengdu, so the last lines about Cao Ba's hard life are also about himself.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像给曹霸写的一篇小传记。开头说他出身高贵，现在却是平民，但他不在乎富贵，只爱画画。接着写他最风光的时候：给凌烟阁功臣重画像，文官武将一个个活了过来，褒公、鄂公好像刚从战场上下来。最精彩的是画玉花骢：画师们都画不像，曹霸用心构思，一会儿就画出一匹“真龙”，画马和真马面对面站着，连养马的人都看呆了。“一洗万古凡马空”一句，把他的画技写到了顶点。然后拿学生韩幹来比，说明曹霸画的是马的骨气和精神。最后笔锋一转：这样的大画家，如今却在战乱中给路人画像，还被人白眼相看。前面越风光，后面越心酸，杜甫对他的同情，也是对自己命运的感叹。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a short life story of Cao Ba. It begins with his noble family and his fall to a commoner, but he does not care about riches; he only loves to paint. Then comes his greatest time. He repaints the portraits of the founding ministers, and the officials and generals come alive again; the Dukes of Bao and E look as if they have just ridden off the battlefield. The best part is the horse Jade Flower. No painter could catch its likeness, but Cao Ba thinks hard and in a moment paints a 'true dragon'. The painted horse and the real horse stand face to face, and even the grooms are stunned. The line 'washing away all the ordinary horses of ten thousand years' lifts his art to its peak. Next, his student Han Gan is set beside him, to show that Cao Ba painted a horse's bone and spirit. At the end the poem turns: this great painter now paints passers-by in a time of war and gets scornful looks. The brighter the past, the sadder the present. Du Fu's pity for Cao Ba is also a sigh about his own fate.
